chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī that he said:
A severe hardship befell me, so I went to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام. I sought permission to enter upon him, and he gave me permission. When I sat down, he said:
O Abū Hāshim, which of Allah’s blessings upon you do you wish to render thanks for?
Abū Hāshim said: I was struck silent and did not know what to say to him. Then he عليه السلام began speaking to me and said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted you iman (faith), by which He has made your body forbidden to the Fire. He has granted you well-being, thereby helping you in obedience. And He has granted you contentment, thereby protecting you from abasement.
O Abū Hāshim, I only began with this because I thought that you wanted to complain to me about the one who caused this to happen to you. I have ordered one hundred dinars for you, so take them.

key_terms.التَّبَذُّلِ: Abasement, humiliation, or loss of dignity through neediness.
key_terms.النَّارِ: The Fire, meaning Hellfire in the hereafter.
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: Faith that protects the believer from the Fire.
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةَ: Well-being and sound condition that enable obedience.
key_terms.الْقُنُوعَ: Contentment with what one has been given.
key_terms.مِائَةِ دِينَارٍ: One hundred dinars given as material assistance.

ai.seo_question: What blessings should a believer remember when facing hardship?
ai.summary: This narration teaches that a believer should first recognize Allah’s greater blessings even in times of hardship: iman (faith), well-being, and contentment. Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Hādī عليه السلام redirects attention from complaint toward shukr (gratitude), while also showing practical care by providing financial support.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5863 - It is narrated from Abu Hashim Al-Jafari that he said:
"I was afflicted with severe hardship, so I went to Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as), peace be upon him. I sought permission to enter, and he granted me permission.
When I sat down, Imam (as) said:
'O' Abu Hashim, which of Allah's (swt) blessings upon you do you wish to fulfill its gratitude?'
Abu Hashim said: I was speechless and did not know what to say.
Then Imam (as), peace be upon him, initiated the conversation and said:
'Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has granted you faith, by which He (swt) has made your body forbidden to the Fire.
He (swt) has granted you well-being, enabling you to obey Him (swt). He (swt) has granted you contentment, protecting you from disgrace.
O' Abu Hashim, I began with this because I thought you were about to complain to me about who has caused this hardship to you. I have ordered for you one hundred dinars, so take them.'"
